![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/80bde6a20ceed7c052a87eda6f05c542f6046de7014f6402f5f453b6610f8d42.png)

Consider the set $A,$ shown above. The boundary of $A$ is given by

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/05b25521109f373e2a7718523ce6289b27b37bd185d4fc60f0d052c232f4f8a4.png)

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the line $y=-1+x.$

Therefore, 

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y=-1+x\,}.
$$
